To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fractional derivative in time of the order α (with 0<α<2) in the governing equation of the dynamics of a curved interface between two coexisting phases with the same chemical potentials leads to a new type of the front motion.

(i) the front velocity depends on its shape; (ii) the shape of the front is not a constant, but depends on time; (iii) the shape of a front depends on the potential function and on the memory kernel; (iv) the shape of an axisymmetric front is a function of time and of a single parameter, while for a non axisymmetric front the shape of a non axisymmetric is described by a function of two parameters.

the dynamics of curved fronts in power law memory materials can be described by a two dimensional fractional in the time partial differential equation, and the equation governing the motion of small curvature front has the same form as the one for a classical front, but the coefficients are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of fronts in systems with long memory and the main results are the following.
the modeling of a curved front between two stable phases in a system with power law memory and with the analysis of the dynamics of a small curvature of such fronts.
a mathematical model of the dynamics of a curved phase boundary in a system with power law memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of curved fronts in the presence of power law memory is qualitatively similar to the corresponding dynamics in the case without memory.
a curved front in the system under consideration is stable for a sufficiently long time, and the front curvature decreases with time.
the dynamics of a small curvature interface in a plane is qualitatively similar to the dynamics of a planar interface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the front is stable if the power law exponent is less than 2 and unstable for larger values.
the dynamics of the fronts in a system with power law memory is qualitatively similar to the dynamics of the same fronts in the corresponding system without memory.
the dynamics of a curved interface is governed by a fractional in time partial derivative equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the memory effects lead to the stabilization of the front.
a small curvature front in systems with power-law memory can be described by an equation of the Burgers type with a non-local term.
the dynamics is strongly influenced by memory effects.
